On Tue, Oct 19, 2027 at 10:05 AM Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We have an internal redline to the Order Form that clarifies "PO acceptance" for automated procurement flows (draft attached).

Thanks for the flag — reviewed the draft. High-level concerns:

1) We cannot treat webhook receipt alone as definitive "acceptance" because it removes required checks for valid purchase authority and could create exposure if itemized billing disputes arise.
2) We can, however, accept a two-step model: (a) webhook receipt signals "PO received" and triggers provisioning, (b) explicit contract-level acceptance occurs when either (i) a signed Order Form is returned or (ii) no dispute is raised within a defined hold period (suggest 72 hours) after receipt.

Suggested language (attached as snippet): legal_suggested_snippet.txt — it keeps provisioning speed but preserves a clear audit trail and dispute window. We should also require that the webhook payload include a unique requester ID and an authorization token verifying the PO came from an authorized account in Ariba.

Karthik — from a procurement/ops perspective, is 72 hours workable? If not, what's the minimal window you can live with operationally and still avoid provisioning attention from improper POs?

Alex Martinez
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_suggested_snippet.txt (txt, 1KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Tom — appreciate the sample fields. Short update and proposed approach so you can run this with Procurement: 

1) Schema: Redwood will provide a compact JSON webhook with PO number, currency, total, line items (sku, qty, unit price), ship-to address, tax breakdown, requester_id, and an auth token. We'll share a full example JSON once legal is aligned.

2) Acceptance model (proposed compromise):
- "PO Received": webhook delivery + 2xx response will be logged as received and will trigger provisioning pipelines.
- "PO Accepted": automatic acceptance occurs if Millennium Health's procurement team does not raise a written dispute within 48 business hours of receipt. During the 48-hour window provisioning can proceed but final billing will be contingent on acceptance.

3) Contract redlines: Alex proposed keeping a 72-hour dispute window; we counter with 48 business hours to reduce provisioning delay while balancing risk. If Legal cannot accept 48 hours, suggest we default to 72 hours.

Next steps:
- Alex to confirm whether the 48-hour window is contract-compliant or if 72 hours is required.
- Grace to provide test endpoint and sample payload to Millennium (Tom) so they can map Ariba fields.
- Karthik to confirm if any procurement gating is required on our side for Ariba registration (supplier id, GL codes).

Tom — can you confirm the Ariba contact who will run the mapping and whether they can be available for a short call tomorrow? Also attached a test payload we plan to use.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
